To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
1) The presence of a single supermassive black hole (SBH) can be inferred from the presence of a low density core, and that the SBH mass can be determined from the core radius.
1. The formation of binary black holes (BBHs) and their coalescence is a major source of gravitational waves (GWs) in the frequency range 10^{-4}-10^{-1} Hz.

(1) single black holes sink in the center of a galactic nucleus, (2) binary black holes eject a large fraction of the stars from their host galaxy, (3) the binary black holes are ejected at velocities of several hundred km/s and (4) the ejected binary black holes may be the progenitors of the hyper-velocity stars observed in the Galaxy
In summary, our research is concerned with
the dynamical evolution of stellar systems in the vicinity of supermassive (10^6 to 10^10 M_sun) black holes, which are thought to reside in the centres of most galaxies.
the dynamical evolution of star clusters, and their interactions with massive compact objects such as supermassive black hole binaries.
the dynamical evolution of star clusters around supermassive BHs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the presence of a supermassive black hole in a galactic nucleus has dramatic consequences for the dynamical evolution of the stellar component.
the dynamics of galactic centers is dominated by supermassive black hole (SMBH) masses and the binary nature of SMBHs.
we have not yet seen the full effects of the formation and evolution of binary black holes in the centers of galaxies, but we have seen enough to know that it is happening.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have found that the dynamics of galactic cores is dominated by supermassive black hole (SBH) binary formation and evolution.
the formation and evolution of galaxies is a dynamical process that involves the formation and evolution (and coalescence) of SBHs.
the presence of SBHs in the nuclei of galaxies is revealed by their effects on the dynamics of the stars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the dynamics of galactic cores is a powerful probe of the formation and evolution of SBHs.
the formation and evolution of galactic nuclei is intimately connected to SBHs.
the dynamics of galactic cores can provide important information about the masses, spins, and orbital parameters of SBHs.
